title: Resolve Linux auto-update permissions and distinguish relay reconnects from revocation.
changes: Pin the supervised Linux launcher's npm prefix to its installed CLI/Node tree so auto-update cannot unexpectedly write into system-owned global modules.
Treat WebSocket 1013 as a potentially transient overload, not proof of deployment, and bound rapid reconnect loops while retaining server-requested capacity delays.
Give revocation (1008) and duplicate-device ownership (1012) precedence over reconnect hints to prevent unauthorized retries and competing agents.
Rate-limit discovery triggered by repeated reconnections without delaying scheduled release/recovery convergence polls.
Retain the previously published hard HTTP/JSON update-manifest deadline and adaptive reconnect helper; include all imported agent modules in the public npm client.
Test Linux service prefix, user-visible reconnect behavior and safe rollout; release a new immutable client/runtime version, never overwrite 0.2.197.
